stages.title: Approach Planview

sections.heading: Approach Planview
paragraphs: Planview는 절차를 To Scale로 나타내며, 항로·fix·navaid·holding·terrain·airspace·missed approach 등 핵심 정보를 번호별로 설명한다.

sections.heading: Approach Planview
paragraphs: p.161의 번호 범례를 아래 원본 이미지에서 확인한다.
Jeppesen 원문 설명: The planview is a graphical “To Scale” depiction of the approach procedure. Latitude and longitude ticks are shown in 10-minute increments along the neatline.

figure.caption: Approach Chart Legend p.161 · Approach Planview

sections.heading: No. 1 · To-scale planview and latitude/longitude ticks
paragraphs: The planview is a graphical “To Scale” depiction of the approach procedure. Latitude and longitude ticks are shown in 10-minute increments along the neatline.

sections.heading: No. 2 · Primary-airport runway layout
paragraphs: Complete runway layouts are depicted for the primary airport.

sections.heading: No. 3 · Approach transitions
paragraphs: Approach transitions are depicted with a medium-weight line; bearing, mileage and associated altitude are placed along the track.

sections.heading: No. 4 · Off-chart origination navaid/waypoint information
paragraphs: Off-chart origination navaid/waypoint name, frequency, identifier and Morse code are shown when required for fix formation.

sections.heading: No. 5 · Cross radials, bearings and DME fix formation
paragraphs: VOR cross radials and NDB bearings used in forming a fix are shown; DME formation distances are shown when applicable.

sections.heading: No. 6 · Airspace fixes and symbols
paragraphs: Airspace fixes are depicted using several different symbols according to usage.

sections.heading: No. 7 · Navaid boxes and DME capability
paragraphs: Navaid boxes include name, identifier, Morse code and frequency; a letter D indicates DME capability and an asterisk indicates part-time.

sections.heading: No. 8 · Substitute fix identification
paragraphs: Substitute fix identification information is located below the facility box when applicable.

sections.heading: No. 9 · IAF and IF labels
paragraphs: Initial Approach Fixes and Intermediate Fixes are labeled as (IAF) and (IF) respectively.

sections.heading: No. 10 · Shadowed primary navaid box
paragraphs: A shadowed navaid box indicates the primary navaid upon which lateral course guidance for the final approach segment is predicated.

sections.heading: No. 11 · Final/intermediate approach course line
paragraphs: The final/intermediate approach course is indicated with a heavy-weight line.

sections.heading: No. 12 · Final approach course bearing
paragraphs: The final approach course bearing is shown in bold text, with a directional arrow as needed.

sections.heading: No. 13 · Airspace fix names / formation information
paragraphs: Airspace fix names are shown near or tied to the fix; formation information is placed below the name.

sections.heading: No. 14 · Jeppesen-derived database identifiers
paragraphs: Jeppesen-derived database identifiers are depicted when different from the State-supplied name.

sections.heading: No. 15 · Missed approach segment
paragraphs: The missed approach segment is shown with heavy-weight dashed line work.

sections.heading: No. 16 · Holding/racetrack patterns
paragraphs: Holding/racetrack patterns are shown with both inbound and outbound bearings; restrictions are charted when applicable.

sections.heading: No. 17 · Terrain high points and man-made structures
paragraphs: Some terrain high points and man-made structures are depicted along with their elevations; generally only high points 400 feet or more above airport elevation are shown.

sections.heading: No. 18 · Highest portrayed high-point arrow
paragraphs: Arrow indicates the highest of the portrayed high points within the planview area only.

sections.heading: No. 19 · Generalized terrain contours
paragraphs: Generalized terrain contours may be depicted based on several geographic factors.

sections.heading: No. 20 · Rivers and large water bodies
paragraphs: Rivers/large water bodies are shown. Smaller and seasonal water areas are not depicted.

sections.heading: No. 21 · Special Use Airspace
paragraphs: Some, but not all, Special Use Airspace boundaries and identifiers are depicted.

sections.heading: No. 22 · Secondary IFR and VFR airports
paragraphs: All secondary IFR airports, and VFR airports that lie under the final approach, are depicted.

sections.heading: No. 23 · Planview charting scale
paragraphs: Charting scale used is indicated along the left side of the planview.

sections.heading: 단계 세부 항목 정리
paragraphs: 이 표는 해당 단계의 원문 기반 문제 항목을 이론 복습용으로 다시 정리한 것이다.

stages.title: RNAV · Insets · Recommended Descent Table

sections.heading: RNAV and non-precision aids
paragraphs: RNAV 절차의 TAA 표기, Not To Scale inset, 비정밀 접근의 Recommended Altitude Descent Table을 학습한다.

sections.heading: RNAV Procedure Differences
paragraphs: p.162의 번호 범례를 아래 원본 이미지에서 확인한다.
Jeppesen 원문 설명: A primary navaid box is shown for RNAV approach procedures augmented by ground-based facilities; system type, channel and system approach ID are shown.

figure.caption: Approach Chart Legend p.162 · RNAV Procedure Differences

sections.heading: No. 1 · RNAV primary navaid box
paragraphs: A primary navaid box is shown for RNAV approach procedures augmented by ground-based facilities; system type, channel and system approach ID are shown.

sections.heading: No. 2 · Terminal Arrival Area / Terminal Area Altitude (TAA)
paragraphs: Some RNAV procedures utilize a TAA; each sector is graphically placed in the planview with the foundational waypoint, forming bearings, arrival altitudes and applicable NoPT labels.

sections.heading: No. 3 · Modified TAA coverage
paragraphs: When normal TAA coverage is modified, segmented areas are depicted with the applicable altitudes indicated.

sections.heading: No. 4 · Database waypoint naming
paragraphs: Due to required database use, only waypoint names are shown; formations and coordinates are omitted.

sections.heading: No. 5 · Along-track distances for unnamed waypoints
paragraphs: Along-track distances, normally to the next named waypoint, are shown per source for unnamed waypoints.

sections.heading: Approach Planview — Not To Scale Insets
paragraphs: p.163의 번호 범례를 아래 원본 이미지에서 확인한다.
Jeppesen 원문 설명: A solid line outlines an inset when information has been removed from the associated “To Scale” tracks; labels inside indicate the use of the contained procedural information.

figure.caption: Approach Chart Legend p.163 · Approach Planview — Not To Scale Insets

sections.heading: No. 1 · Solid-line inset
paragraphs: A solid line outlines an inset when information has been removed from the associated “To Scale” tracks; labels inside indicate the use of the contained procedural information.

sections.heading: No. 2 · Dashed-line NOT TO SCALE inset
paragraphs: A dashed line outlines an inset when information remains in line with the associated “To Scale” tracks; a NOT TO SCALE label is included inside the inset.

sections.heading: Non-Precision Recommended Altitude Descent Table
paragraphs: p.163의 번호 범례를 아래 원본 이미지에서 확인한다.
Jeppesen 원문 설명: The Recommended Altitude Descent table is sequenced in the same direction as the flight tracks in the profile; a gray arrow indicates left-to-right or right-to-left direction.

figure.caption: Approach Chart Legend p.163 · Non-Precision Recommended Altitude Descent Table

sections.heading: No. 1 · Table direction / gray arrow
paragraphs: The Recommended Altitude Descent table is sequenced in the same direction as the flight tracks in the profile; a gray arrow indicates left-to-right or right-to-left direction.

sections.heading: No. 2 · DME checkpoint source navaid
paragraphs: The source for DME checkpoints is indicated by the navaid ident; when Jeppesen-derived, DME is used whenever possible.

sections.heading: No. 3 · Recommended-altitude row label
paragraphs: The row of recommended altitudes is labeled to indicate its associated use with the VDA.

sections.heading: No. 4 · DME checkpoint distance
paragraphs: The DME distance defining each checkpoint is depicted in whole and tenths of a nautical mile.

sections.heading: No. 5 · Recommended altitude at each checkpoint
paragraphs: A recommended altitude, defined by a position along the VDA at a given point, is supplied for each checkpoint.

sections.heading: No. 6 · Distance-to-fix checkpoint
paragraphs: When DME is not available, each checkpoint is defined by distance to a fix along the final approach course, shown in whole and tenths of a nautical mile.

sections.heading: No. 7 · “To” waypoint for checkpoint
paragraphs: The “to” waypoint is indicated when checkpoints are defined by a distance to a fix.

sections.heading: No. 8 · Non-precision qualifier in combined approaches
paragraphs: When a non-precision approach is combined with a precision approach, a qualifier indicates that the recommended altitudes relate to the non-precision approach only.

sections.heading: No. 9 · Bold FAF altitude
paragraphs: Bold text indicates that the altitude is charted in the FAF altitude box within the Briefing Strip.

No. 4 · DME checkpoint distance

No. 5 · Recommended altitude at each checkpoint

No. 6 · Distance-to-fix checkpoint
Jeppesen 원문 설명: When DME is not available, each checkpoint is defined by distance to a fix along the final approach course, shown in whole and tenths of a nautical mile.
No. 7 · “To” waypoint for checkpoint
Jeppesen 원문 설명: The “to” waypoint is indicated when checkpoints are defined by a distance to a fix.
No. 8 · Non-precision qualifier in combined approaches
Jeppesen 원문 설명: When a non-precision approach is combined with a precision approach, a qualifier indicates that the recommended altitudes relate to the non-precision approach only.
No. 9 · Bold FAF altitude
Jeppesen 원문 설명: Bold text indicates that the altitude is charted in the FAF altitude box within the Briefing Strip.

stages.title: Approach Profile View · 1–18

sections.heading: Approach Profile View
paragraphs: Profile View는 final/intermediate segment를 Not To Scale로 표현하며 altitude, course, navaid, procedure turn, FAP, runway 관련 표기법을 설명한다.

sections.heading: Approach Profile View — Conventions
paragraphs: p.164의 번호 범례를 아래 원본 이미지에서 확인한다.
Jeppesen 원문 설명: All procedure bearings are shown. Bold text emphasizes the Final Approach Course; arrowheads are added as needed to indicate direction of flight.

figure.caption: Approach Chart Legend p.164 · Approach Profile View — Conventions

sections.heading: No. 1 · Procedure bearings and direction arrows
paragraphs: All procedure bearings are shown. Bold text emphasizes the Final Approach Course; arrowheads are added as needed to indicate direction of flight.

sections.heading: No. 2 · Bearing placement relative to track
paragraphs: Bearings are placed either above, below, or inset in the track.

sections.heading: No. 3 · Holding/racetrack inbound and outbound bearings
paragraphs: Both inbound and outbound bearings are depicted for procedure holding/racetrack patterns.

sections.heading: No. 4 · Minimum altitudes in profile view
paragraphs: All altitudes depicted in the profile view are minimum altitudes unless specifically labeled otherwise; altitudes are above mean sea level in feet.

sections.heading: No. 5 · Maximum altitude notation
paragraphs: Maximum altitudes may be abbreviated “MAX”.

sections.heading: No. 6 · Mandatory altitudes
paragraphs: Mandatory altitudes are shown without abbreviations.

sections.heading: No. 7 · Recommended altitudes
paragraphs: Recommended altitudes are shown without abbreviations.

sections.heading: No. 8 · Bold FAF/FAP procedure altitude
paragraphs: Bold text emphasizes the procedure altitude at the FAF or the glide-slope intercept altitude at the FAP/FAF; this is also the altitude shown in the Briefing Strip.

sections.heading: No. 9 · Navaid type / Morse code / glide-slope crossing altitude
paragraphs: The type of navaid is indicated; identifying Morse code is shown for all markers, and glide-slope crossing altitudes are included when known.

sections.heading: No. 10 · Navaid ident/name and crossing altitude
paragraphs: The navaid ident or name is included where confusion may occur; associated crossing altitudes are included when applicable.

sections.heading: No. 11 · Fix names and DME formations
paragraphs: All fix names are shown along with any DME formations; the source DME ident is included when multiple DME sources are charted.

sections.heading: No. 12 · Standalone DME name
paragraphs: Standalone DME names are depicted similar to named waypoints.

sections.heading: Approach Profile View — Detailed Elements 1–18
paragraphs: p.164의 번호 범례를 아래 원본 이미지에서 확인한다.
Jeppesen 원문 설명: Procedure notes that relate directly to information portrayed in the profile view are charted within the profile view, normally in upper right or left corners.

figure.caption: Approach Chart Legend p.164 · Approach Profile View — Detailed Elements 1–18

sections.heading: No. 1 · Profile-view procedure notes
paragraphs: Procedure notes that relate directly to information portrayed in the profile view are charted within the profile view, normally in upper right or left corners.

sections.heading: No. 2 · Broken navaid/fix symbol
paragraphs: A “broken” navaid or fix symbol indicates that it does not fall directly in line with the final approach track.

sections.heading: No. 3 · Procedure-turn outbound bearing
paragraphs: Outbound bearings associated with procedure turns are included for situational awareness.

sections.heading: No. 4 · Procedure-turn minimum altitude
paragraphs: Minimum altitude while executing the procedure turn.

sections.heading: No. 5 · Procedure-turn remain-within distance
paragraphs: The distance to remain within while executing the procedure turn, measured from the initiating navaid unless otherwise indicated.

sections.heading: No. 6 · Profile-view ground line
paragraphs: The profile-view ground line represents an imaginary straight line originating from the runway threshold; no terrain high points or man-made structures are represented in the profile view.

sections.heading: No. 7 · Procedure flight track
paragraphs: Procedure flight tracks are portrayed using a thick solid line; multiple separate procedures using the same altitudes are represented by a single line.

sections.heading: No. 8 · Final Approach Point (FAP)
paragraphs: Final Approach Point (FAP), beginning of the final approach segment for precision approaches.

sections.heading: No. 9 · NM distance to zero point
paragraphs: Nautical-mile distance to the “0” point; not included at DME fixes.

sections.heading: No. 10 · NM distance between navaids/fixes
paragraphs: Nautical-mile distance between two navaids and/or fixes.

sections.heading: No. 11 · Final Approach Course bearing
paragraphs: Final Approach Course bearing; repeated only if a change in course occurs.

sections.heading: No. 12 · Relative track placement by crossing altitude
paragraphs: Tracks are placed relative to each other based on the corresponding crossing altitudes.

sections.heading: No. 13 · Non-precision track deviating from GS/VDA
paragraphs: Non-precision procedure flight tracks that deviate from the Glide Slope and/or Vertical Descent Angle are depicted as a dashed line.

sections.heading: No. 14 · DA/MDA or GS/VDA descent-limit pull-up
paragraphs: Pull-up representing the DA/MDA or when reaching the descent limit along the GS/VDA.

sections.heading: No. 15 · Non-CDFA pull-up arrow
paragraphs: Pull-up arrow associated with a non-precision approach not using a CDFA technique.

sections.heading: No. 16 · TDZ/runway-end/threshold elevation
paragraphs: Touchdown-zone, runway-end, or threshold elevation labeled accordingly.

sections.heading: No. 17 · Threshold Crossing Height (TCH)
paragraphs: Threshold crossing height associated with the charted glide slope or vertical descent angle.

sections.heading: No. 18 · Runway block
paragraphs: Runway block symbolizing the runway; the approach end represents the runway threshold.

paragraphs: 이 표는 해당 단계의 원문 기반 문제 항목을 이론 복습용으로 다시 정리한 것이다.

sections.heading: Profile holding/RNAV and supporting boxes

paragraphs: Time limit applicable to the outbound leg of the procedure holding/racetrack.

paragraphs: Minimum altitude while executing the procedure holding/racetrack.

sections.heading: No. 21 · Holding/racetrack inbound and outbound bearings
paragraphs: Outbound and inbound bearings associated with the procedure holding/racetrack.

sections.heading: No. 22 · RNAV waypoint ident
paragraphs: RNAV waypoints are identified by their five-character identifier only.

sections.heading: No. 23 · Segment Minimum Altitude (SMA)
paragraphs: Segment Minimum Altitudes are represented by a shaded rectangle bordered by the two defining fixes; the minimum altitude is shown along the top edge of the sector.

sections.heading: No. 24 · Altitudes corresponding to VDA
paragraphs: Altitudes that correspond to the VDA.

sections.heading: No. 25 · Top-of-Descent distance to next fix
paragraphs: Nautical miles to the next fix are supplied for the “Top of Descent” when not at a fix.

sections.heading: No. 26 · VDA pull-up at DA/MDA
paragraphs: Pull-up along the VDA at the DA/MDA is depicted relative to the missed approach point.

sections.heading: No. 27 · Along-track distance “to” fix
paragraphs: Nautical miles and name of “to” fixes are supplied for all along-track distance fixes.

sections.heading: No. 28 · VNAV path FAF to LTP/TCH
paragraphs: A dotted gray line illustrates the VNAV path from the FAF to the Landing Threshold Point (LTP) TCH.

sections.heading: No. 29 · Visual flight track before runway threshold
paragraphs: Visual flight track is shown when the missed approach point is prior to the runway threshold.

sections.heading: No. 3 · Non-precision VDA and descent rates
paragraphs: For non-precision approaches, Vertical Descent Angle is shown, when applicable, in degrees along with relative descent rates in feet per minute.

sections.heading: No. 4 · MAP distance and timing
paragraphs: The location of the Missed Approach Point is defined; distance and associated timing are included only when applicable.

sections.heading: No. 5 · Approach/visual slope/REIL lighting
paragraphs: Installed approach lights, visual approach slope indicators, and runway end identification lights (REIL) are depicted for the straight-in landing runway.

sections.heading: No. 6 · Missed approach icons
paragraphs: Missed approach icons symbolize the final “up and out” actions associated with the missed approach procedure; complete instructions are shown textually in the Briefing Strip.

sections.heading: No. 1 · Landing minimums regulation label
paragraphs: Minimums label indicates that landing minimums comply with a specific regulation, but never below State-published values.

sections.heading: No. 2 · Expanded circle-to-land area indicator
paragraphs: Indicates that the published Circle-To-Land minimums are based on TERPS 8260.3B change 21 or later; expanded circling approach areas apply where depicted.
